q: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities, that have only magnitude, are called ____.
e: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities, that have only magnitude, are called scalar quantities. Scalar quantities here means a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: However, some quantities have a directional quality. Not only the magnitude but also the direction is required for the complete description of such quantities. These quantities, that have both magnitude and direction, are called ____.
e: However, some quantities have a directional quality. Not only the magnitude but also the direction is required for the complete description of such quantities. These quantities, that have both magnitude and direction, are called vectors. The physics in this sentence is built around vectors.

q: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type, such as A, F, v, s. In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing ____ on the top of their symbols.
e: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type, such as A, F, v, s. In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing arrows on the top of their symbols. The physics in this sentence is built around arrows.

q: The magnitude of F is written as ____.
e: The magnitude of F is written as F = |F|. The physics in this sentence is built around F = |F|.

q: A = B: A and B are equal in magnitude and have the ____.
e: A = B: A and B are equal in magnitude and have the same direction. Same direction here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: A = -B: A and B are equal in magnitude but have ____.
e: A = -B: A and B are equal in magnitude but have opposite directions. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite directions.

q: A = 2B: The magnitude of A is two times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is the ____ as that of B.
e: A = 2B: The magnitude of A is two times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is the same as that of B. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: A = -3B: The magnitude of A is three times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is ____ to that of B.
e: A = -3B: The magnitude of A is three times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is opposite to that of B. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite.

q: Using graphical method a vector may be represented by an ____. The length of the arrow is proportional to the magnitude of the vector and the direction of the arrow gives the direction of the vector.
e: Using graphical method a vector may be represented by an arrow. The length of the arrow is proportional to the magnitude of the vector and the direction of the arrow gives the direction of the vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: To add A and B, first draw A. Then draw B in such a way that the tail of B is at the tip of A. Then draw a third vector R from the tail of A to the tip of B. R is the vector sum A + B and it is called the ____.
e: To add A and B, first draw A. Then draw B in such a way that the tail of B is at the tip of A. Then draw a third vector R from the tail of A to the tip of B. R is the vector sum A + B and it is called the resultant vector.

q: A + B = B + A. Vector addition is ____.
e: A + B = B + A. Vector addition is commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: In algebraic notation, A − B = A + (−B). Hence, vector subtraction is not ____.
e: In algebraic notation, A − B = A + (−B). Hence, vector subtraction is not commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called ____ of a vector, and the new vectors obtained are called vector components of the original vector.
e: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called resolution of a vector, and the new vectors obtained are called vector components of the original vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two ____ components, namely, horizontal component and vertical component.
e: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two perpendicular components, namely, horizontal component and vertical component. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ.
e: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ. The physics in this sentence is built around $A_x = A \cos \theta$, $A_y = A \sin \theta$.
